claims.text: LaCr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2O3−δ is a high-entropy perovskite containing five equiatomic B-site transition-metal cations.
Coexisting transition-metal cations enable dynamic redox interplay among multiple metal sites.
The dynamic redox interplay modulates d-orbital coupling.
Modulated d-orbital coupling optimizes adsorption energies of key OER intermediates.
The high-entropy perovskite has higher OER current density than the proposed physical mixture of single-B-site perovskites.
The high-entropy perovskite is more durable than the physical-mixture control.
Epitaxial films can provide closely matched crystallographic facets, morphology, and surface termination for comparison of the high-entropy oxide with parent perovskites.
A physical mixture of LaCrO3, LaMnO3, LaFeO3, LaCoO3, and LaNiO3 can be fabricated as an epitaxial-film control with identical facet orientation and surface termination.
Multiple transition metals in the high-entropy perovskite change valence upon adsorption of reaction intermediates.
In-situ XPS and XAS would evidence a dynamically modulated distribution of oxidized and reduced transition-metal sites.
DFT-derived d-band-center adjustments support the proposed change in d-orbital coupling.
Multiple transition-metal cations interact synergistically in the high-entropy perovskite.
The multication interaction creates a flexible electronic environment that fine-tunes adsorption and desorption energies of OER intermediates.
Fine-tuning OER-intermediate binding accelerates electron transfer.
The (001) high-entropy perovskite exhibits 17- to 680-fold higher current at fixed overpotential than its individual single-B-site parent compounds.
The high-entropy perovskite should show distinct mixed-oxidation-state dynamics relative to the physical-mixture control.
The high-entropy system should have a more optimal d-band-center alignment than the physical-mixture control.
The high-entropy system should have enhanced electron density near the Fermi level relative to the physical-mixture control.
Controlling crystallographic facet and morphology helps isolate an intrinsic composition–activity relationship.
